report_name: New 'OperTraitor' Tool Exposes Excessive RBAC Risks in Kubernetes

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Groups
attack_patterns.description: Enabled by overly permissive operators, attackers can query the Kubernetes API to discover the permissions of a compromised operator's service account.

attack_patterns.name: Default Accounts
attack_patterns.description: An operator's service account, when compromised, can be abused as a valid, privileged account to perform malicious actions within the cluster.

attack_patterns.name: Container API
attack_patterns.description: An operator with broad permissions can be used to read Kubernetes secrets containing credentials, tokens, and other sensitive data by interacting with the container API.

attack_patterns.name: Container and Resource Discovery
attack_patterns.description: A compromised operator with sufficient permissions can be used to discover other resources, pods, and services running within the Kubernetes cluster.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Attackers can exploit the inherent trusted relationship between the Kubernetes API server and a compromised, highly-privileged operator to execute malicious actions.

tools.name: OperTraitor
tools.description: An open-source, LLM-powered tool released by Unit 42 to audit Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) configurations of Kubernetes operators and identify excessive permissions.

tools.name: kubectl
tools.description: The Kubernetes command-line tool, which can be used by an attacker to enumerate cluster role bindings and other resources after compromising an operator.

tools.name: krane
tools.description: An open-source tool mentioned as an alternative for auditing Kubernetes RBAC permissions.

tools.name: rakkess
tools.description: An open-source tool mentioned as an alternative for auditing Kubernetes RBAC permissions.

tools.name: OPA/Gatekeeper
tools.description: A policy-as-code tool recommended for enforcing RBAC best practices in Kubernetes to mitigate risks from overly permissive operators.

tools.name: Kyverno
tools.description: A policy-as-code tool recommended for enforcing RBAC best practices in Kubernetes to mitigate risks from overly permissive operators.

vulnerabilities.name: Excessive RBAC Permissions in Kubernetes Operators
vulnerabilities.description: A class of vulnerability where Kubernetes operators are granted overly permissive RBAC roles, such as wildcard permissions or cluster-wide access to sensitive resources like secrets, creating potential backdoors that can be exploited if the operator is compromised.

identities.name: OperatorHub
identities.description: A public registry for Kubernetes operators, identified as a supply chain weakness for hosting outdated and overly permissive operators that users can easily deploy.

identities.name: Prometurbo
identities.description: A Kubernetes operator from IBM, used as a case study. An outdated version on OperatorHub had excessive wildcard permissions, and a more recent version still had a ClusterRole allowing it to read all secrets in the cluster.

identities.name: Kubernetes
identities.description: The container orchestration platform whose operator and RBAC security posture is the subject of the research.

identities.name: Unit 42
identities.description: The threat intelligence team at Palo Alto Networks that released the OperTraitor tool and conducted the research on Kubernetes operator risks.

identities.name: IBM
identities.description: The vendor of the Prometurbo operator, whose GitHub repository contained a more recent but still overly permissive version of the operator.

indicators.name: Kubernetes Cluster-Wide Secret Listing
indicators.pattern:
title: Kubernetes Cluster-Wide Secret Listing
id: 2b8c1f9d-5e6a-4b7c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects API requests to list or watch all secrets in a Kubernetes cluster, a high-risk action often associated with privilege escalation or data theft. This rule should be run against Kubernetes API server audit logs.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-29
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/agentic-ai-kubernetes-operator-risks/
tags:
  - attack.t1552.007
level: high
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem: '/api/v1/secrets'
    cs-method: 'GET'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects attempts to list or watch all secrets in a Kubernetes cluster, a high-risk action often associated with privilege escalation or data theft, as described in the hunting hints.

indicators.name: Kubernetes RBAC Enumeration via Kubectl
indicators.pattern:
title: Kubernetes RBAC Enumeration via Kubectl
id: 9e0f1a2b-3c4d-4e5f-8b7c-6d5e4f3a2b1c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of kubectl to enumerate cluster-wide role bindings, a common reconnaissance technique for discovering permissions.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-29
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/agentic-ai-kubernetes-operator-risks/
tags:
  - attack.t1069.003
  - attack.t1613
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/kubectl'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'get'
      - 'clusterrolebindings'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the `kubectl get clusterrolebindings` command, a common reconnaissance technique for discovering permissions within a Kubernetes cluster.
